title: The Missing Necklace
content:
Detective Emma arrived at the old hotel early in the morning.

A valuable necklace was missing.

She looked around the room and asked the hotel manager:

“What happened here?”

The manager looked nervous.

“The necklace disappeared last night,” he said.

Emma took out her notebook.

“When did it disappear?”

“Around ten o’clock.”

“Who was in the hotel at that time?”

“There were four guests and two employees.”

Emma walked to the window.

“Where was the necklace before it disappeared?”

“It was inside a small box on that table.”

She looked at the empty box carefully.

Then she noticed something strange.

A small key was on the floor.

“Whose key is this?” Emma asked.

Nobody answered.

She decided to speak to the guests.

The first guest was a young artist.

“What were you doing at ten o’clock?” Emma asked.

“I was painting in my room.”

The second guest was an old businessman.

“Why were you near the hotel garden last night?”

“I couldn't sleep,” he replied.

Emma continued asking questions.

“Which room were you staying in?”

“Room 12.”

Finally, she spoke to the hotel cleaner.

“How did you enter the room this morning?”

“With my master key,” the cleaner answered.

Emma looked at the small key again.

Suddenly, she smiled.

“I know who took the necklace.”

Everyone looked surprised.

The necklace was not stolen by a guest.

The hotel manager had taken it.

“But why?” the manager asked nervously.

“Because you needed money,” Emma replied. “And how do I know? This key belongs to your private office.”

The manager looked down.

The mystery was solved.

Emma closed her notebook.

For a good detective, the right answer always begins with the right question.
